name: Split Hero Asymmetric
description: Broken-grid hero with image left and copy right offset by 32px vertical misalignment — one column wider than the other.
use_cases: SaaS product launch, luxury brand, portfolio
anti_patterns: Avoid on data-heavy dashboards where information density matters. Don't overuse for multiple sections.
examples: Stripe.com homepage | Linear.app homepage | Vercel.com homepage | Coinbase homepage

name: Full Bleed Hero with Overlay
description: Edge-to-edge background image/video with text overlay at bottom-left. Text reads over gradient scrim.
use_cases: Creative agency, film portfolio, luxury brand
anti_patterns: Ensure text contrast over image (WCAG AA). Don't use without mobile fallback.
examples: Apple.com iPhone pages | Netflix.com | Spotify.com year-end campaign

name: Centered Text Hero
description: Copy and CTA centered vertically and horizontally. Background is solid color or subtle gradient.
use_cases: SaaS landing page, newsletter signup, product launch
anti_patterns: Add enough whitespace (200px+ top/bottom). Don't put too much text — max 2 lines of copy.
examples: Notion.so homepage | Slack.com homepage | GitHub.com homepage

name: Animated Text Hero
description: Text morphs, types, or transitions on load. Can include rotating headlines or typewriter effect.
use_cases: Product showcase, creative agency, portfolio
anti_patterns: Keep animation under 3 seconds. Don't auto-play without purpose. Don't use on mobile if janky.
examples: Apple.com product pages | Raycast.com homepage | Linear changelog page

name: Bento Grid Features
description: Cards arranged in uneven grid with varying sizes — some 2x, some 1x. Asymmetric but intentional.
use_cases: Feature showcase, product landing, pricing comparison
anti_patterns: Don't make all cards same size (that's just a grid). Keep visual hierarchy clear.
examples: Apple.com MacBook/iPhone features | Linear.app features | Snapchat.com app features

name: Staggered Card Flow
description: Cards overlap slightly or are offset diagonally. Creates sense of depth and movement.
use_cases: Creative features showcase, portfolio, agency
anti_patterns: Don't overlap text content. Only overlap decorative elements or card edges.
examples: Discord.com Nitro features | Notion.so features | Calm.com features

name: Side-by-Side Feature
description: Two-column layout: image/illustration on one side, copy on other. Alternates per feature row.
use_cases: SaaS features with screenshots, dashboard preview
anti_patterns: Alternate left/right placement per row. Don't repeat same layout 3+ times.
examples: Stripe.com features | Figma.com features | Linear features

name: Scroll-Triggered Animation
description: Content reveals on scroll — fade up, slide in, parallax layers. Adds depth to long pages.
use_cases: Feature walkthrough, product story, portfolio
anti_patterns: Don't animate everything (pick 3-5 key moments). Don't use parallax on mobile.
examples: Apple.com product pages | Stripe.com homepage | Spotify.com Wrapped

name: Feature Stack Vertical
description: Full-width cards stacked vertically with consistent 80px spacing. Each card has headline + description.
use_cases: Long-form feature pages, documentation, landing
anti_patterns: Don't exceed 5 stack items. Add visual break (illustration, screenshot) every 2-3 items.
examples: Notion.so features | GitHub.com features | Atlassian features

name: Pricing 3-Tier Grid
description: Three cards side-by-side with middle card highlighted (border, size, or color). Most common pattern.
use_cases: SaaS pricing comparison, service tiers
anti_patterns: Middle card must be visually elevated. Don't make all three identical. Add annual/monthly toggle.
examples: Stripe.com pricing | Linear pricing | Vercel.com pricing

name: Feature Comparison Table
description: Horizontal table with checkmarks and feature names. Rows for features, columns for plans.
use_cases: Complex pricing with many features, enterprise sales
anti_patterns: Don't use for <5 features (use cards instead). Don't hide important features below fold.
examples: GitHub.com pricing | Atlassian pricing | Shopify.com pricing

name: Simple 2-Tier
description: Only two options side by side. One is recommended. Reduces decision paralysis.
use_cases: Simple service offerings, consultation pricing
anti_patterns: Make the recommended option visually obvious. Don't add a third option just because.
examples: Stripe.com simple pricing | Cal.com pricing | Ghost.org pricing

name: Social Proof Carousel
description: Horizontal scrolling logos or testimonials. Auto-scrolls or user-swipes. Logos in grayscale.
use_cases: Building trust before pricing CTA, enterprise landing
anti_patterns: Keep auto-scroll slow (30s+). Don't use blurry logos. Don't exceed 12 logos.
examples: HubSpot.com | Freshworks.com | Intercom.com

name: Testimonial Feature Block
description: Single large testimonial with photo, name, title. Full-width block between sections.
use_cases: High-converting landing pages, authority building
anti_patterns: Use real headshots (not stock). Keep quote under 200 chars. Don't use generic praise.
examples: Apple.com customer stories | Stripe.com user stories | Shopify.com merchants

name: Case Study Card
description: Card with company logo, result metric, and 2-sentence summary. Links to full case study.
use_cases: B2B landing pages, SaaS conversion pages
anti_patterns: Include specific metric (not just 'improved'). Don't use unnamed companies.
examples: HubSpot.com case studies | Salesforce.com stories | Notion.so customer stories

name: Logo Wall (Grayscale)
description: Dense grid of customer/company logos in grayscale. No color. Uniform sizing.
use_cases: Enterprise landing pages, investor decks
anti_patterns: Grayscale only — color logos clash. Don't include tiny logos. Don't use competitors' logos.
examples: Stripe.com customer logos | Linear.app customers | GitHub.com customers

name: Editorial Longform
description: Full-width typography-driven layout. Wide body text (680px max-width) with generous line-height.
use_cases: Blog posts, brand storytelling, content pages
anti_patterns: Don't use for app UIs. Max-width must be 680-720px for readability.
examples: Medium.com | Substack.com | Apple Newsroom

name: Masonry Grid
description: Cards arranged in Pinterest-style columns with varying heights. No strict row alignment.
use_cases: Gallery, portfolio, image showcase, product catalog
anti_patterns: Don't use for text-heavy content. Keep card widths consistent even if heights vary.
examples: Pinterest.com | Unsplash.com | Dribbble.com

name: Sidebar Navigation
description: Fixed sidebar (240-280px) with main content area. Sidebar has nav items, possibly collapsible.
use_cases: Dashboard, admin panel, complex app with many sections
anti_patterns: Don't make sidebar wider than 300px. Collapsible on mobile. Group related items.
examples: Notion.so | Linear.app | Figma.com | GitHub.com

name: Top Navigation Bar
description: Fixed header (64-80px) with logo left, nav center, CTA right. Transparent on hero, solid on scroll.
use_cases: Landing pages, marketing sites, most SaaS apps
anti_patterns: Don't hide nav on scroll. Don't use hamburger for <6 items. Add backdrop-blur on scroll.
examples: Vercel.com | Stripe.com | Linear.app

name: Sticky Section (Scroll Spy)
description: Section that stays fixed while other content scrolls over it. Used for product tours or comparisons.
use_cases: Product comparisons, interactive demos, long pages
anti_patterns: Don't use on short pages. Keep fixed section under 100vh. Don't block content.
examples: Apple.com iPhone comparison | Linear changelog | Stripe documentation

name: Full-Width Image Section
description: Full-bleed image with text overlay or adjacent text. No container constraints.
use_cases: Brand storytelling, photography portfolio, product showcase
anti_patterns: Ensure image has text variant for contrast. Don't stretch low-res images.
examples: Apple.com product pages | Nike.com editorial | Samsung.com product pages

name: Bento Dashboard
description: Multi-size card grid for dashboard overview. KPIs large, charts medium, lists small.
use_cases: Analytics dashboards, admin panels, monitoring tools
anti_patterns: Don't overload with data. Keep consistent card spacing. Use consistent chart style.
examples: Linear.app dashboard | Vercel.com analytics | Grafana dashboards

name: Sidebar + Content
description: Left sidebar (200-260px) for navigation, right content area. Sidebar may have user info at bottom.
use_cases: Complex apps with nested navigation, settings pages
anti_patterns: Don't use for 3-level navigation (add breadcrumbs). Collapsible sidebar for content-heavy.
examples: Figma.com | Slack.com desktop | GitHub.com repository view

name: Command Palette Layout
description: Full-screen overlay with centered search bar and command list. Keyboard-first interaction.
use_cases: Power user tools, creative apps, developer tools
anti_patterns: Don't make the only way to navigate. Add keyboard shortcut indicator. Show recent commands.
examples: Linear.app | Notion.so | Raycast.com | Figma.com

name: Settings Panel
description: Form-based settings in left tab list + right content panel. Categories on left, fields on right.
use_cases: User settings, admin, configuration pages
anti_patterns: Don't put all settings on one scroll. Group logically. Add save/discard for dirty state.
examples: GitHub.com settings | Notion.so settings | Stripe.com dashboard settings

name: Content Footer
description: Multi-column footer with link groups, social icons, copyright. Background darker than main content.
use_cases: Every landing page, marketing site
anti_patterns: Don't make footer an afterthought. Include legal links. Don't use tiny text (<12px).
examples: Stripe.com footer | Vercel.com footer | Linear.app footer

name: Sticky Footer CTA
description: Bottom bar (fixed or sticky) with CTA button that stays visible while scrolling. Used for conversion.
use_cases: Landing pages, pricing pages, sign-up flows
anti_patterns: Don't use on short pages (<3 screen heights). Don't cover content on mobile. Max-height 80px.
examples: Cal.com booking | Stripe.com pricing signup | Linear.app pricing

name: Side CTA Block
description: Full-width colored block with CTA on one side and copy on other. Used as section break between content sections.
use_cases: Newsletter sign-up, trial offer, feature highlight
anti_patterns: Don't use more than 2 per page. Don't use same color for every CTA block.
examples: Linear.app changelog CTA | Notion.so upgrade block | HubSpot.com demo CTA

name: Inline CTA (Contextual)
description: Small CTA button placed within content — at end of feature description or after testimonial.
use_cases: Long-form landing pages, blog posts, feature pages
anti_patterns: Don't make it bigger than the primary CTA. Keep it relevant to surrounding content.
examples: Stripe.com feature sections | Linear.app feature pages | Notion.so docs pages

name: Single-Step Form
description: Single form with 3-5 fields, visible labels, inline validation. Clean layout with clear CTA.
use_cases: Newsletter signup, contact form, simple registration
anti_patterns: Don't exceed 5 fields. Don't use placeholder-only labels. Don't hide error messages.
examples: Stripe.com checkout | Linear.app signup | Cal.com booking

name: Multi-Step Wizard
description: Progress indicator at top, one logical group per step, back/next navigation. State preserved on back.
use_cases: Onboarding flows, complex signup, checkout, profile setup
anti_patterns: Don't lose state on back. Don't skip progress indicator. Don't allow jump-ahead without validation.
examples: Stripe.com onboarding | Notion.so setup | Figma.com onboarding

name: Inline Validation Form
description: Real-time validation on blur (not keystroke). Error below field. Success checkmark.
use_cases: Settings forms, profile editing, any form with async validation
anti_patterns: Don't validate on keystroke (noisy). Don't show errors before user interacts. Don't use red for everything — use semantic colors.
examples: GitHub.com settings | Linear.app settings | Vercel.com dashboard

name: File Upload Zone
description: Drag-and-drop zone with dashed border. File type + size validation. Preview for images. Progress bar for uploads.
use_cases: Profile avatar, document upload, media management
anti_patterns: Don't accept files without validation. Don't upload without progress feedback. Don't allow multiple uploads without queue management.
examples: Notion.so file upload | Figma.com file import | Dropbox.com upload

name: Split-Screen Auth
description: Left panel: brand imagery/headline. Right panel: auth form. 50/50 or 60/40 split.
use_cases: SaaS signup, premium products, branded experiences
anti_patterns: Don't use stock photos. Don't make form too wide (>400px). Don't hide social login below fold.
examples: Linear.app login | Vercel.com login | Stripe.com login

name: Centered Card Auth
description: Centered card (max-width 400px) on neutral background. Logo top, form middle, social login bottom.
use_cases: Most SaaS apps, internal tools, admin panels
anti_patterns: Don't make card too wide. Don't use colored background that clashes with brand. Don't forget 'forgot password' link.
examples: Notion.so login | GitHub.com login | Slack.com login

name: Passwordless Auth
description: Email-only input. Magic link or OTP sent. No password field. Clear instructions after submit.
use_cases: Modern SaaS, developer tools, low-friction signup
anti_patterns: Don't reveal whether email exists. Don't auto-submit on enter without confirmation. Don't forget to mention 'check your email' with spam folder hint.
examples: Linear.app passwordless | Raycast.com login | Vercel.com login

name: Progress Stepper
description: Numbered steps (1/5, 2/5...) at top. Current step highlighted. Back/Next at bottom.
use_cases: Setup wizards, profile completion, multi-step forms
anti_patterns: Don't skip step numbers. Don't make steps non-clickable (allow jump-back). Don't lose progress on refresh.
examples: Stripe.com onboarding | Notion.so setup | Linear.app onboarding

name: Interactive Tutorial
description: Overlay tooltips pointing to UI elements. 'Next' button advances. 'Skip' always visible.
use_cases: Feature discovery, new user walkthrough, complex app introduction
anti_patterns: Don't block entire UI. Don't show on every visit. Don't make tooltips too long. Always allow skip.
examples: Figma.com tutorial | Intercom.com onboarding | Product tour examples

name: Checklist Sidebar
description: Fixed sidebar with 4-6 items. Checkmarks on completion. Progress percentage. CTA for next incomplete item.
use_cases: Dashboard onboarding, account setup, feature adoption
anti_patterns: Don't show completed items as disabled. Don't auto-remove completed items (user wants to see progress). Don't make checklist block main content.
examples: Linear.app sidebar | Notion.so onboarding | Vercel.com dashboard

name: Mega Menu
description: Dropdown with multiple columns. Categories, links, possibly featured content. Keyboard navigable.
use_cases: Enterprise sites, complex products, multi-section marketing
anti_patterns: Don't trigger on hover alone (add click/tap). Don't make it too wide (>800px). Don't hide sub-categories without visual cue.
examples: GitHub.com nav | Atlassian nav | Notion.so nav

name: Mobile Bottom Sheet
description: Slide-up panel from bottom. 3-5 options with icons. Drag handle at top. Tap outside to dismiss.
use_cases: Mobile navigation, action menus, filter panels
anti_patterns: Don't use for primary navigation (use bottom tab bar). Don't make content scrollable inside sheet (keep it short). Don't forget drag handle affordance.
examples: Linear.app mobile | Figma.com mobile | iOS native patterns

name: Toast Stack
description: Small cards at bottom-right or top-right. Auto-dismiss in 3-5s. Stacked vertically. Success/error/info variants.
use_cases: Action feedback, success confirmation, non-critical alerts
anti_patterns: Don't stack more than 3. Don't auto-dismiss errors (require manual dismiss). Don't use for critical alerts (use modal instead).
examples: Linear.app toasts | Vercel.com notifications | Notion.so toasts

name: Notification Center
description: Dropdown or sidebar panel. Grouped by date. Unread indicator badge. Mark all as read.
use_cases: Activity feeds, team updates, system alerts
anti_patterns: Don't show unread count >99 (show '99+'). Don't auto-refresh without visual cue. Don't mix notification types without grouping.
examples: GitHub.com notifications | Linear.app inbox | Slack.com activity

name: Illustration + CTA
description: Centered illustration (simple, on-brand). Headline explaining what goes here. CTA to take action.
use_cases: No data yet, first-time experience, cleared state
anti_patterns: Don't use complex illustrations (keep it simple). Don't use 'Nothing here' without explanation. Don't forget the CTA — user needs next step.
examples: Linear.app empty states | Notion.so empty pages | Vercel.com empty dashboard

name: Search + Suggestion
description: Search bar at center. Below: suggested actions or popular content. Helps user find what they need.
use_cases: Search results, filtered views, discovery pages
anti_patterns: Don't show zero results without alternatives. Don't make search the only option (add suggestions). Don't forget to clear previous search state.
examples: GitHub.com empty repos | Linear.app search | Figma.com community

name: Data Table with Filters
description: Table with sortable columns. Filter bar above. Pagination or infinite scroll. Row hover highlight.
use_cases: Admin panels, list views, data management
anti_patterns: Don't make columns too narrow. Don't hide filters behind a button (show them). Don't use pagination >100 pages (switch to search).
examples: GitHub.com repos list | Linear.app issues | Stripe.com payments

name: Stat Cards Row
description: 3-5 cards in a row. Each: number (large), label (small), trend indicator (up/down arrow).
use_cases: Dashboard overview, KPI display, analytics summary
anti_patterns: Don't use more than 5 cards. Don't make numbers too small (<24px). Don't forget trend direction (up = good/green, down = bad/red).
examples: Linear.app dashboard | Vercel.com analytics | Stripe.com dashboard

name: Timeline / Activity Feed
description: Vertical timeline with timestamps. Each entry: icon, title, description, time. Alternating or left-aligned.
use_cases: Activity logs, changelog, audit trail
anti_patterns: Don't use for >50 items without virtual scrolling. Don't make timestamps too prominent (use relative time). Don't forget to handle 'loading more' state.
examples: GitHub.com commit history | Linear.app activity | Notion.so page history

name: AI Chat Interface
description: Full-height chat layout with message bubbles, streaming text area, typing indicator, tool-use cards, input bar fixed at bottom. User messages right-aligned, AI left-aligned with avatar. Tool results in expandable cards.
use_cases: AI copilots, customer support chat, developer tools, knowledge bases, agent interfaces
anti_patterns: Don't use for single-turn Q&A (use FAQ). Don't make chat bubbles full-width (distinguish user/AI). Don't hide input on scroll.
examples: ChatGPT.com | Claude.ai | Linear.app AI | Cursor.com AI panel

name: Kanban Board
description: Drag-and-drop columns (To Do / In Progress / Done). Cards with title, assignee, priority badge. Column header with count. Add card button per column. Drag handle on cards.
use_cases: Project management, task tracking, sprint planning, content calendars, hiring pipelines
anti_patterns: Don't use for lists >5 columns. Don't skip mobile adaptation (stack to accordion). Don't make cards too dense.
examples: Trello.com | Linear.app boards | Notion.so kanban | Jira boards

name: Command Palette (Full)
description: Centered modal with search input at top. Results grouped by category below. Keyboard navigation (↑↓ to select, Enter to execute). Recent searches. Fuzzy match highlighting.
use_cases: Power-user navigation, quick actions, file search, component search, universal search
anti_patterns: Don't make results too small. Don't skip keyboard navigation. Don't show >10 results without scrolling.
examples: Linear.app ⌘K | Vercel.com ⌘K | Raycast.com | Figma.com ⌘K

name: Map-Centric Layout
description: Map takes 70-80% viewport. Overlay panels for details (sliding from bottom or side). Search bar floating over map. Pin markers with clustering. List/map toggle.
use_cases: Delivery tracking, real estate, ride-hailing, local business finder, event discovery, travel planning
anti_patterns: Don't make map smaller than 60% viewport. Don't skip map loading state. Don't use without mobile GPS fallback.
examples: Google Maps | Uber.com | Airbnb.com/map | Zillow.com

name: Data Grid / Spreadsheet
description: Table with sortable columns, resizable headers, inline editing, cell selection, row hover, bulk actions toolbar, column visibility toggle, export button.
use_cases: CRM data, inventory management, financial spreadsheets, admin panels, analytics tables
anti_patterns: Don't use for <10 rows (use cards instead). Don't skip keyboard navigation for editing. Don't hide sort indicators.
examples: Airtable.com | Google Sheets | Notion.so databases | Retool.com grids

name: Media Player / Audio
description: Album art / video thumbnail, play/pause/skip controls, progress bar with seek, volume control, fullscreen toggle, playlist sidebar, now-playing bar.
use_cases: Music streaming, podcast apps, video platforms, webinar replay, audio content
anti_patterns: Don't make controls too small (48px touch targets). Don't skip keyboard shortcuts (space=pause, arrows=seek). Don't hide volume.
examples: Spotify.com | YouTube.com | SoundCloud.com | Apple Music

name: Before/After Slider
description: Side-by-side images with draggable divider. Slider handle in center. Labels (Before/After) positioned top corners. Touch-friendly handle size (48px+).
use_cases: Photography portfolios, renovation showcases, fitness transformations, product comparisons, design iterations
anti_patterns: Don't use without touch support. Don't make divider handle too small. Don't skip mobile (switch to stacked tabs).
examples: Webflow.com features | Apartment Therapy before-after | Fitness app transformations

name: Multi-Panel / Split View
description: 2-3 resizable panels side by side. Panel dividers draggable. Collapse/expand per panel. Minimum width per panel with overflow scroll. Responsive: stack on mobile.
use_cases: IDE layouts, email clients (inbox+compose), documentation+preview, file managers, design tools
anti_patterns: Don't use on mobile (stack to single panel). Don't skip panel resize handles. Don't make min-width too small (<200px).
examples: VS Code | Slack.com | Apple Mail | Figma.com panels

name: Accordion / FAQ
description: Vertically stacked collapsible sections. Each: header (clickable) + content (expandable). Only one open at a time or multiple. Chevron rotation indicator. Smooth height animation.
use_cases: FAQ pages, product documentation, support sections, feature details, legal/terms
anti_patterns: Don't use for primary navigation (use menu). Don't skip animation (jarring open/close). Don't hide all content by default on mobile.
examples: Stripe.com/docs | Tailwind CSS docs | Apple.com support | Government sites

name: Sticky Sidebar + Scrollspy
description: Left sidebar fixed while content scrolls. Active section highlighted in sidebar based on scroll position. Smooth scroll to section on sidebar click. Sidebar collapses on mobile.
use_cases: Documentation sites, long-form articles, portfolio case studies, API references, changelogs
anti_patterns: Don't use with >15 sections (use collapse). Don't skip scrollspy tracking. Don't hide sidebar without toggle on mobile.
examples: Tailwind CSS docs | Stripe.com docs | React.dev | MDN Web Docs
